title: Seishun Buta Yarou wa Odekake Sister no Yume wo Minai
content:
Let me preface by saying. I forgot how annoying Kaede was.

This is besides the emotional tides that this movie brings, her archetype has been a tired stereotype of these types of stories that it just does not hit as hard any more.

Not gonna lie, having not watched any Bunny Girl Senpai content for such a long time, it was refreshing to see the bickering couple, Sakuta and Mai. Of course, I had forgotten a lot about the series that this movie was able to remind me of twinkles here and there, using small dialog hints. No stretched copy-pasted flashback or any unnecessary tangents.

Away from thecouple. Kaede is the focus of this movie, which is questionable to say the least. The overly attached Imouto is in frenzy, trying to gain some self confidence and overcome her insecurities while Sakuta acts as the supportive big brother of course. Classic. All meanwhile the puberty syndrome stills lurks around him, Sakuta finds himself running laps around his struggling sister and this mysterious dream he had.

I feel there is nothing much to say without spoiling it all. The movie took its time. Silent moments, slow transitions, persisting conflict. It did not rush its steps at all, which is good narratively, but also very painful in terms of pacing.

One thing for sure. The visuals were stunning and the English dub was not half bad at all.
Overall: 7.6/10.
